cycle_position.summary: Hotels: RevPAR accelerating (Q2 2026 +5.7% as ADR +4.4%; HVS raised its 2026 forecast to +3.0%), convention demand rebounding. Cap rates: ~8.5% overall average, Q1 2026 transactions 8.6%, Q2 print 7.7% on an upscale mix shift (T12 through June 8.2%). STRs: the regulatory ratchet keeps tightening — registration caps, licensing limits, zoning restrictions spreading; platform data-sharing mandates (e.g. SB 346 eff. Jan 1, 2026) end under-the-radar operation; NYC allows sub-30-day stays only with the host on site (max 2 guests); San Francisco requires permanent residency and caps unhosted nights.

supply_demand.value: Hotel demand growth outpacing supply in 2026; STR supply growth constrained by regulation in exactly the urban East Coast markets this buyer works.

debt_terms.value: Hotel debt = SBA 504/7(a) for small flagged/independent assets; STR financed as investor residential (DSCR lenders underwrite STR income with haircuts).

small_investor_verdict.entry_vehicle: Only defensible form at $1-2M: an STR-zoned property in a resort/leisure market with EXPLICITLY permissive local rules verified in writing. Urban East Coast STR is a compliance trap; small hotels are operating businesses, not real estate plays.
small_investor_verdict.reasoning: The regulatory direction is uniformly hostile in the buyer's core markets (DC/MD/VA and the I-95 cities), platform data-sharing removes the gray zone, and an STR-dependent underwrite can be destroyed by one council vote — the exact opposite of the exemption-anchored certainty the core strategy is built on.

gaps: Jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction STR rules for DC/MD/VA beach + mountain markets (the one viable niche) — not yet screened
